fr.title: Grospiron lâche la présidence du comité d’organisation des JO-2030
fr.description: Lecture zen Les JO-2030, un champ de bosses devenu infranchissable pour Edgar Grospiron. - AFP Le comité d’organisation des Jeux olympiques et paralympiques 2030 a annoncé la démission de son président, Edgar Grospiron, plombé par une grave crise de gouvernance et qui avait perdu la confiance des parties prenantes de ces JO d’hiver. « Sa décision de quitter la présidence s’inscrit dans une transition choisie, organisée et assumée, dans l’intérêt du projet et de sa gouvernance. Elle traduit une volonté partagée avec les parties prenantes de permettre à l’organisation d’entrer rapidement dans cette nouvelle phase opérationnelle » , a indiqué le Cojop d’Alpes-2030 dans un communiqué. Et l’organisme de préciser qu’une assemblée générale, prévue lundi prochain, « sera l’occasion d’organiser l’intérim, jusqu’à la désignation prochaine d’une ou d’un nouveau président » . « Après plusieurs mois de tension au niveau de la gouvernance, je tire la conclusion que les conditions ne sont plus réunies pour moi de continuer cette aventure » , a écrit de son côté l’ancien champion olympique de ski de bosses (Jeux d’Albertville-1992) sur son profil LinkedIn. « Certains diront sans doute que c’est un échec ou un renoncement. Je préfère dire que j’ai atteint, dans le cadre qui était le mien, le point où il devenait plus juste de passer la main que de s’y accrocher. Oui, il y a eu des obstacles. Oui, il y a eu des accrochages. Oui, il y a eu des décisions difficiles à prendre » , a ajouté l’Aindinois de 57 ans. Têtu En décembre, la démission de la directrice des opérations, Anne Murac, avait marqué le début d’une série noire de départs qui allait culminer avec celui du n° 2 de l’instance, l’Ardennais Cyril Linette , annoncé en pleins Jeux d’hiver de Milan-Cortina et justifié par des « désaccords insurmontables » avec Grospiron. Mission d’inspection générale, recommandations d’un ancien de Paris-2024, intérim de l’ex-préfet Michel Cadot puis arrivée du préfet Vincent Roberti comme nouveau directeur général : aucun remède n’aura réussi à remettre la gouvernance sur de bons rails. Et les bonnes nouvelles du début d’été – dévoilement des emblèmes, annonce d’EDF comme premier sponsor premium, bouclage de la carte des sites olympiques – n’auront pas réussi à sauver le siège de celui qui a dû affronter également des luttes d’influence politique et des crispations avec certains acteurs en région vivant mal la volonté de certains responsables parisiens de transplanter dans leurs territoires de montagne l’expérience des JO-2024. Sa gestion managériale et sa vision de la gouvernance sont aussi pointées par ses détracteurs, qui le décrivent comme « n’en faisant qu’à sa tête » et « n’écoutant rien ». Mis en ligne le 10/09/2026 à 19:22 Grospiron lâche la présidence du comité d’organisation des JO-2030 Sa position était devenue intenable : Edgar Grospiron a été contraint de démissionner de ses fonctions de chef du Cojop d’Alpes-2030, jeudi 10 septembre 2026. Ou l’échec d’une reconversion trop acrobatique pour le médaillé d’or olympique des bosses en 1994 à Albertville.

ph.title: GMOs and science
ph.description: AS a result of high food prices in the country due to our low farm productivity, the incidence of stunting among Filipino kids aged 0 to 5 years old has risen. The latest figure by the Food and Nutrition Research Institute under the Department of Science and Technology showed that stunting incidence rose to 25.3 in 2025 from 23.6 percent in 2023, a figure that falls within the World Health Organization range as a high public health concern. We all know that stunting at this age group has serious repercussions on the future of the country. Medical doctors have revealed that around 90 percent of the individual’s brain is formed during the ages 0 to 5 years old. Deprived of the necessary nutrients during that age bracket, an individual’s brain cannot develop to its full potential. There is a strong possibility of permanent cognitive disability for those who suffered stunting at this critical age group. This reality is now manifesting in the results of cognitive tests among Filipino pupils aged 10 years. The World Bank noted that 9 out of 10 Filipino children belonging to this age group cannot read or understand simple text by the end of their primary school. If this trend continues given that poverty remains widespread in the country, we will face the prospect of raising a nation of morons. The solution is to increase food production and make nutritious food available and affordable, particularly to poor consumers. But it will take some time before this objective is achieved. Dr. Howard Bouis, a World Food Prize awardee (the equivalent of a Nobel Prizein agriculture) and an emeritus fellow of the International Food Policy Research Institute, recommends the alternative of packing a country’s staple food with vitamins or nutrients. This will necessitate a change in plant breeding technology not just in terms of producing varieties that raise productivity but more importantly, increasing the density of a crop’s nutrient contents. He noted that this was achieved in Pakistan, where wheat, its staple food, had “a high-yielding, high zinc content accounting for about one-half of the domestic wheat production.” Bouis added that the technology is not new considering that there are already “more than 500 million people in poor countries [who] are eating grain enriched with single selected nutrients through plant breeding.” As I pointed out in my past essays in this paper, what Bouis is advocating is not new in the Philippine agricultural landscape. We have Golden Rice for more than a decade but its widespread adoption and production have been stymied by legal complications. Golden Rice is packed with vitamin A, a nutrient wherein many Filipino consumers suffer deficiency. We all know that the vitamin is essential in maintaining good eyesight, immune function and reproductive health. Through genetic engineering (modification), our plant breeders were able to produce a rice variety packed with vitamin A. Being the staple food of the Filipinos, it was intended to alleviate vitamin A deficiency among the consumers, particularly the poor. However, so-called environmentalists have vigorously objected that since Golden Rice is a genetically modified organism (GMO), it is unnatural and therefore poses a risk to the environment and human health. The protesters brought the matter to the attention of a court that rendered a verdict based on what it referred to as “precautionary principle.” This requires that proponents of the GMO product must first prove that the new crop poses no harm to the environment and public health before allowing its widespread propagation and consumption. Golden Rice proponents argue that demanding a 100-percent guarantee that the product is environmentally safe is simply unreasonable. Any scientific invention necessarily carries its own risk. On the other hand, the application of pesticides and inorganic fertilizers is not prohibited despite their proven harmful effects on the environment and human health if excessively used. What matters is the degree of the risk involved versus the potential benefits to the public in the introduction of the new technology. GMO adoption in the country and worldwide is already widespread. GMO wheat is cultivated in Pakistan and so is GMO corn and soybean, and to a limited degree, rice, in China. In addition, Bouis noted a report from Nature Scientific Reports that documented “farmers, consumers, those working in rice processing and retailing, and local government officials were primarily accepting and excited by the prospects of producing and consuming Golden Rice to improve nutrition.” My issue with environmentalists During my tenure as a senior official of the Department of Agriculture (DA), I was also faced with the same challenge on whether the agency should promote Golden Rice given vociferous protestations from so-called environmentalists and pro-farmers groups. As head of the DA’s policy and planning unit, my office’s position was critical in determining what the policy direction of the agency should be vis-à-vis the issue of GMOs. I refused then to cater to populist demagoguery and asked for solid empirical proofs from anti-GMO groups to support their claim. Beyond incidental anecdotal evidence and generalizations, none from the objectors’ rant can really come out with robust scientific evidence to support their position. I then asked the protesters if they were injected with Covid-19 vaccines as it was the peak of the pandemic then. Practically all of them admitted that they were injected with Covid-19 vaccines. Curiously, Covid-19 vaccines are products of genetic engineering or modification. I then pointed out to the anti-GMO group that it is the height of absurdity to accept and promote Covid-19 vaccines that are genetically modified products to Filipinos but not the ingestion of a GMO crop. This case clearly illustrates how some of our policymakers who are sympathetic to the anti-GMO group opted to base their decision on populist sentiment rather than science. And this is a major contributing factor why our agriculture sector has significantly lagged behind neighboring countries that have adopted a science-based decision-making in the formulation of their policies and plans. There is urgency in settling the issues on GMO crops if we are to embark in intensifying production of crops that can help address malnutrition and vitamin-deficiency among the Filipino consumers. Currently, there is a collaborative effort between the International Rice Research Institute and the Philippine Rice Institute to produce HIZR, a biofortified rice innovation designed to address iron and zinc deficiencies among Filipino consumers. With HIZR, zinc and iron intakes can increase by 25 percent, at no extra cost to the family. The money would partly pay for data centres with a capacity of up to one gigawatt, Berlin said, and an “Investment Council” would be set up to boost business links between the two nations. The Gulf is a key source of capital for the AI boom as oil-rich states in the region seek to invest their energy wealth. “The UAE invests for the long term and builds partnerships that endure,” UAE Industry Minister Sultan Ahmed Al Jaber said. “Germany has been an important strategic and economic partner for decades and the additional 40 billion euros intended investment reflects our ambition to invest in that relationship.” Berlin had earlier rolled out the red carpet for President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, who met Chancellor Friedrich Merz after earlier being received with military honours by President Frank-Walter Steinmeier. Security was tight for the visit, with Berlin cordoning off flag-lined streets and deploying large numbers of police. The visit comes as the US war against Iran has roiled the Gulf region, with President Donald Trump’s erratic diplomacy unsettling many midsize powers and leading them to diversify their strategic and economic partnerships. Merz visited the Gulf region in February, shortly before the US-Israeli war started against Iran. He said then that “we need such partnerships more than ever at a time when major powers are increasingly dominating politics”. The UAE is Germany’s largest trading partner in the Gulf, with bilateral trade topping $15 billion last year, and many big German companies have a presence there including BMW, Siemens, ThyssenKrupp and rail operator Deutsche Bahn. German and Emirati companies had signed a further 29 agreements with a total value of 9.4 billion euros during the visit, Berlin said. The UAE meanwhile has made major investments in Germany, including in the chemical industry and offshore wind power. During Merz’s visit in February, German energy giant RWE and Abu Dhabi’s national oil company ADNOC signed a memorandum of understanding on LNG imports over the next decade. Gulf countries have also long bought defence equipment from Germany and have shown interest in start-ups that make drones to bolster NATO’s deterrence efforts against Russia. Germany, the largest EU economy, supports talks towards a European Union free trade deal with the Emirates.

pk.title: Pakistan can turn rooftop solar boom into ‘swarm grids’: study
pk.description: Pakistan can harness its growth in rooftop solar through decentralised, community-driven “swarm grids”, but regulatory reform remains the key missing link between technical feasibility and large-scale deployment, according to a new study. The Policy Research Institute for Equitable Development (PRIED) on Thursday launched a techno-economic assessment of swarm electrification attended by policymakers, regulators, energy experts and civil society representatives. Swarm grids are organic, bottom-up micro-grids built by interconnecting decentralized solar home systems or small renewable energy units without requiring a central master controller. The research comprises two publications: Harnessing Pakistan’s Solar Revolution: A Techno-Economic Assessment of Swarm Electrification, which examines the feasibility of swarm grids in urban and rural settings, and Swarm Grids: The Next Phase of the Solar Boom, which proposes a transition agenda and implementation roadmap. Pakistan’s solar expansion has largely been driven by households, farmers and businesses seeking reliable and affordable electricity rather than by government policy. According to the study, more than 50 gigawatts of solar panels have been imported against around 41GW of installed generation capacity nationwide. Despite the rapid expansion of distributed solar, however, blackouts, brownouts and prolonged load-shedding continue in many areas. The study argues that the central problem is increasingly one of coordination rather than generation capacity. Millions of rooftop solar systems operate as isolated assets instead of being integrated into a coordinated electricity resource. PRIED defines a swarm grid as a digitally coordinated, decentralised local electricity network through which households and businesses can consume their own solar power, store electricity, sell surplus electricity to neighbours and purchase power from nearby prosumers, while using the national grid primarily as a backup. Unlike conventional microgrids, which generally operate within fixed boundaries, swarm grids can allow households and clusters to join, leave or trade electricity dynamically. The researchers tested the concept against two contrasting settings: Islamabad as an urban case, with relatively dense and diverse demand on an established grid, and Tharparkar in Sindh as a rural case characterised by dispersed communities and seasonal agricultural and pastoral livelihoods. The assessment used household surveys, solar-resource data and an hourly dispatch model to examine the technical, economic and institutional feasibility of the model, as well as the willingness of communities to participate. The study found that swarm grids are technically feasible in both urban and rural areas, although their economic models would differ. Urban swarm grids could potentially operate as commercially viable, privately financed businesses, while rural projects would require targeted upfront investment and community capacity-building because of higher initial costs and lower energy density. The research identified the regulatory framework as the most significant common obstacle. Under the existing system, peer-to-peer electricity trading and third-party sales within the territory of a distribution company are restricted. The study says new regulations would be required to determine who can sell electricity, at what price and through what settlement mechanism. Without such changes, it argues, swarm grids are unlikely to progress from feasibility studies to large-scale commercial deployment. The second publication proposes short-, medium- and long-term measures for regulators, including the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (NEPRA) and the Independent System and Market Operator (ISMO), distribution companies, provincial governments and development finance institutions. The recommendations include introducing regulations for peer-to-peer electricity trading, standardising solar equipment connected to distribution networks, opening the retail electricity market under the Competitive Trading Bilateral Contract Market (CTBCM), and launching urban and rural pilot projects. The transition plan also proposes measures aimed at making the shift more inclusive for women. These include allowing solar assets to be registered in the name of either spouse by default, ensuring women are included in installation and handover processes, and supporting women-led operations and maintenance teams.

ae.description: TORONTO , Sept. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Manulife has appointed Sarah Chapman as Global Chief Marketing & Customer Experience Officer , effective January 1, 2027, reporting to Phil Witherington, President and Chief Executive Officer, and joining Manulife's Executive Leadership Team. Manulife appoints Sarah Chapman as Global Chief Marketing & Customer Experience Officer Chapman will lead Manulife's Global Marketing organization, with responsibility for the company's brand, marketing and enterprise customer experience strategies. "Sarah is a proven global leader with deep knowledge of our business, customers and enterprise strategy," said Phil Witherington, President and Chief Executive Officer, Manulife. "Her appointment reflects the strength of our internal talent pipeline and is the result of thoughtful succession planning. I'm confident her strategic perspective, creativity and strong track record of leading transformation will help us build on our momentum, deepen our customer focus and advance Manulife's ambition to be the number one choice for customers." Chapman currently serves as Chief Marketing Officer for Manulife Canada and leads the company's global Digital, Customer Centricity and Sustainability agendas. She previously served as Chief Marketing Officer for Manulife Wealth and Asset Management. Her leadership experience spans marketing strategy, brand, digital, analytics, customer experience and sustainability. "I'm honoured to take on this role and am excited to help make lives better for more than 37 million customers around the world," said Chapman. "Manulife has an exceptional Global Marketing team, a trusted brand, and a clear commitment to innovation. I look forward to building on our strong foundation and working with colleagues across the company to deliver meaningful experiences and impact for our customers." Chapman succeeds Karen Leggett, who will retire from Manulife at the end of this year, providing for a smooth leadership transition. About Manulife Manulife Financial Corporation is a leading international financial services provider, helping customers make their decisions easier and lives better. With our global headquarters in Toronto, Canada, we operate as Manulife across Canada, Asia and Europe, and primarily as John Hancock in the United States. ae.title: Fanttik Expands Automotive and DIY Lineup with New Luma K10 Apex Dash Cam, O11 Pro Circular Saw and More
ae.description: LOS ANGELES , Sept. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fanttik, a leading innovator in high-performance, portable power tools, today announced a new lineup of automotive and DIY tools, led by the Luma K10 Apex 4K dual-channel dash cam and O11 Pro mini cordless circular saw . The new products expand Fanttik's lineup with solutions for everyday driving, home projects, and precision work. New Automotive Tools For drivers, Fanttik is introducing a new dash cam and compact roadside tools designed to help capture the road and handle common emergencies. Luma K10 Apex: Clearer Imaging, Faster Access The Luma K10 Apex is a 4K dual-channel dash cam designed to help drivers capture clearer footage, access recordings more easily, and feel more confident on the road. It features a 4K front camera and 2K rear camera, AI-enhanced image processing, 5.8GHz Wi-Fi 6 connectivity, GPS recording, and a 2.8-inch touchscreen. AI-Powered Imaging for Real-World Driving Luma K10 Apex pairs a 4K front camera powered by the Sony STARVIS 2 IMX678 with a 2K rear camera. An AI NPU and advanced ISP image processing engine work together to optimize image quality across changing road and lighting conditions. Ultra-Fast Access to Recorded Footage With 5.8GHz Wi-Fi 6 connectivity and a companion app, Luma K10 Apex enables wireless preview and 4K footage downloads at speeds over 20 MB/s. Flexible Control on the Road Drivers can manage the camera through a 2.8-inch IPS touchscreen, physical smart control dial, or companion app, making it easy to review footage and adjust settings on the go. Beyond 10 Apex & X11 Pro+: More Than a Tire Inflator The Beyond 10 Apex combines a car jump starter, tire inflator, power bank, and LED flashlight in a 1.44-pound package roughly the size of a soda can. It can jump-start vehicles with up to 7.0L gasoline or 5.0L diesel engines and inflate an R15 tire from 28 to 33 PSI in one minute. The X11 Pro+ features 39s Jet-Inflate performance, topping off an R15 tire in just 39 seconds. With a maximum pressure of 150 PSI, it can handle compact cars, motorcycles, bicycles, and more. New Home DIY Tools Beyond the road, Fanttik's latest releases also include a range of tools for home DIY projects, covering cutting, precision crafting, cleanup, and measurement. O11 Pro: Compact Cutting for Home Projects The Fanttik O11 Pro is a 3-3/8-inch mini cordless circular saw built for woodworking, furniture projects, and home renovation. At just 2.31 pounds and 10.75 inches long, it is easy to use one-handed, maneuver in tight spaces, and carry. Powered by a 4,500 RPM brushless motor, the O11 Pro delivers up to 1 inch of cutting depth. Its built-in CellCore battery provides enough power to cut more than 100 pieces of 1×8-inch lumber per charge. Pix 3 Master: Pen-Style Detail Sander Once the cutting is done, smaller details often need a lighter touch. The Fanttik Pix 3 Master is a pen-style electric detail sander designed for 3D printing, model making, crafts, and precision sanding. Its brushless motor delivers reciprocating sanding at up to 6,000 SPM, while the pen-style grip and ring LED light improve control and visibility around gaps, grooves, and corners. B11 Mix Pro : Powerful Cleaning and Airflow DIY projects can leave plenty of dust and debris behind. The Fanttik B11 Mix Pro's 160W brushless motor delivers up to 130,000 RPM and 70 m/s air speed, helping clear dust, debris, and buildup from hard-to-reach areas. Beyond dust removal, it also includes an axial fan attachment for switching from blowing to cooling, and can inflate pool floats and other inflatables. Neo A11 Pro: Precise Laser Measuring For accurate measurements, the Fanttik Neo A11 Pro features a 165-foot range and 2.4-inch IPS touchscreen. It supports single, continuous, area, and volume measurements, with an angle sensor and universal bubble level to help reduce tilt errors. It delivers ±1/16-inch accuracy and stores up to 30 measurement groups. Luma K10 Apex (12V Car Charger Kit version): Available on Amazon U.S. in October 2026. Other new products: Available now on Amazon U.S. and the Fanttik Official Website. ae.title: Azuki TCG’s Second Set, Fractured Domains, Lands Nov. 20
ae.description: In Brief: Fractured Domains (AZK-02), the second Azuki TCG set, has been announced by Azuki Labs with a Nov. 20, 2026 release date. The debut set, Gates Awakened (AZK-01), carried 148 cards and reached retail June 26 on the back of more than $1 million in presale orders. Its timing falls between the opening Garden Arena regional season and the 2027 Azuki Invitational, and sits inside a roadmap calling for four additional sets over 18 months. A second set is on the way for Azuki TCG. In a post unveiling the expansion, the official Azuki TCG account said Fractured Domains — set code AZK-02 — is dated for Nov. 20, 2026. The announcement arrived without a card count, pricing, presale window or product configuration. Amplifying it, the main Azuki account offered only one line: "On November 20, you will wield the power of two domains..." On November 20, you will wield the power of two domains... Azuki TCG set 2 has been announced ↓@AzukiView on X ↗ Roughly three weeks before the reveal came a teaser whose entire text was "Something new, coming in set 2..." In the replies, fans guessed the set would revolve around a deck featuring the sisters Rei — who battles under the name Raizan — and Shao. Neither sister is named in the teaser or the announcement. What set one established Retail copies of Gates Awakened arrived June 26 with a 148-card lineup: four Leaders, four Gates, a single IKZ resource card, one IKZ token, 54 commons, 33 uncommons, 22 rares, 12 super rares, 15 regular alternate arts, and two portrait rare alternate arts serving as the chase. A booster display is priced at $119.99 and holds 24 packs of 12 cards each, with six boxes per case. Alongside them came four starter decks at $12.99 apiece — Raizan on Lightning, Shao on Water, Bobu on Earth and Zero on Fire — each containing 63 cards and eight foils. The presale campaign cleared $1 million. According to Xu, every milestone was reached with two days still on the clock, so all four exclusive promo cards were included with every order placed. Before that, a March 27 community pre-order offered a randomly selected Shao or Raizan Alpha Starter Deck bundled with booster packs and Alpha-stamped cards for $95 in ANIME. A match takes roughly 20 minutes. Each player assembles a 50-card deck alongside a Leader, a Gate and 10 IKZ cards, then works to reduce the opposing Leader's HP to zero on a two-row board divided between the Alley and the Garden. Competitive calendar November's date comes on the heels of the game's first regional season. The inaugural Garden Arena Regional took place Aug. 15 in Pasadena, California, with CoreTCG hosting and $10,000 in cash prizing on the line, plus stamped prize cards, Seasonal Points and 16 invitations to the 2027 Azuki Invitational. The event sold out. Play consisted of eight rounds of best-of-one Swiss, then three rounds of top cut. Organized play has already required intervention: Rushfire Gate was banned from official Azuki TCG events as of Aug. 18 at 12:01 a.m. PT. A Midwest Regional is set for the fourth quarter of 2026, though its date, venue, registration details and prizing have yet to be announced. Xu had previously spelled out the order of events, describing the plan as "regionals this fall, Set 2 later this year, and an invitational tournament in early 2027," supported by a $100,000 organized play investment. Four more sets across 18 months are planned, per Azuki Labs. The rest of the IP Cards aren't the only release this quarter. On Sept. 8, Azuki Labs said AZUKI — an original manga from Arnold Tsang, formerly character art director on Overwatch — debuts Sept. 17 at 9 a.m. PDT, free on Azuki.com, with fresh chapters landing the third Thursday of every month. A cinematic trailer accompanies chapter one. Its premise hinges on the very Gates that give the card game its name. After Shao's sister Rei vanishes beyond them, Shao's search draws her into a conflict that endangers both worlds. Authentication, grading and encapsulation services from CGC now cover Azuki TCG cards. Azuki first revealed it was building a trading card game on Feb. 12, 2025. "5 months ago I wrote about Azuki building a world before the story," Xu said. "Since then Azuki TCG launched, 300+ players showed up for our first regional, and next month @steamboy33's manga begins. Azuki is becoming a world you can play, read, collect, and make part of your identity."

وخطفت المطية "الفركية" لمالكها القطري ناصر المسند لقب الشوط الرئيسي والأول، وكأس مهرجان ولي العهد للهجن لفئة اللقايا "بكار - مفتوح" بتوقيت بلغ 7:30.718 دقيقة إضافة لظفرها بالتوقيت الأفضل.

ووسط تألق للهجن الإماراتية، ذهب لقب الشوط الثاني وكأس مهرجان ولي العهد "قعدان - مفتوح " للمطية "أديب"
لمالكها مانع الشامسي بتوقيت بلغ 7:24.798 دقيقة، لقب الشوط الثالث وكأس مهرجان ولي العهد "بكار - عام" للمطية "السايحه" لمالكها أحمد الشامسي بتوقيت بلغ 7:35.599 دقيقة، لقب الشوط الرابع وكأس مهرجان ولي العهد "قعدان ـ عام" للمطية "شباب" لمالكها سعيد الكتبي بتوقيت 7:26.243 دقيقة.

وفي الفترة الصباحية، فرضت الهجن السعودية سيطرتها على منافسات الفترة الصباحية، حيث شهدت منافسة محتدمة بين ملاك الهجن من مختلف دول مجلس التعاون الخليجي عبر 15 شوطاً، تميزت بمستويات قوية وأرقام قياسية، بمشاركة واسعة بلغت 496 مطية.

وانتزعت الهجن السعودية صدارة المشهد بتحقيقها المركز الأول في 8 أشواط، تلتها الهجن الإماراتية التي حصدت المركز الأول في 5 أشواط، فيما نالت الهجن القطرية صدارة شوطين.

وأقيم اليوم 23 شوطاً بواقع 15 شوط عام، 4 أشواط مفتوحة، و4 أشواط على كأس مهرجان ولي العهد، بمشاركة 652 مطية، وسط حضور جماهيري.

وعزز المهرجان من تواجده على الصعيد الدولي بمشاركة كبيرة من ملاك الهجن في العالم العربي والدولي؛ إذ يهدف إلى تأصيل تراث الهجن وتعزيز الثقافة السعودية، فيما حقق المهرجان عوائد اقتصادية كبيرة، من خلال تنظيم فعاليات متنوعة تدعم الموروث التراثي، وتعزز الحفاظ عليه وتنميته، ما يعكس العمق الحضاري للمملكة.

mg.title: CIRCULATION - Les taxis-bicyclette s’imposent dans les rues
mg.description: Les taxis-bicyclette sont de plus en plus visibles dans la capitale. Ce mode de transport séduit principalement par son coût attractif. Les taxis-bicyclette envahissent les rues de la capitale. Ils se faufilent entre les véhicules à toute heure pour transporter passagers et marchandises, tout en élargissant constamment leur périmètre. Si leur usage a débuté à Anosizato et Anosibe il y a quelques années, ces cyclotaxis stationnent ou roulent désormais à Anosy et s’aventurent jusqu’au centre-ville (Ambohijatovo, Analakely), atteignant même Antanimena et Ankorondrano. « Nos clients ne se limitent plus à Anosy. Certains demandent à aller jusqu’à Analakely, voire Ankorondrano », témoigne Franck, qui exerce ce métier depuis plusieurs années. Ce mode de transport séduit principalement par son coût attractif. De nombreux usagers se tournent vers cette alternative pour sa rapidité sur de courtes distances, notamment dans les zones à forte congestion. Pour les conducteurs, ce travail représente une source de revenus accessible nécessitant un investissement minime. « Nous n’avons d’autre dépense que le versement quotidien de 15 000 ariary », lance Ezra, lui-même cyclotoxiste. Beaucoup y voient un moyen d’échapper au chômage. Interrogations L’expansion du secteur soulève toutefois des interrogations. L’absence de réglementation claire inquiète certains observateurs, qui pointent du doigt les risques liés à la sécurité routière, le manque de contrôle technique du matériel ou la concurrence avec les transports formels. « Ils roulent au milieu de la chaussée où circulent des véhicules à moteur à une vitesse largement supérieure à la leur», alerte Hery, un automobiliste. D’autres usagers de la route signalent également que la plupart d’entre eux ne maîtrisent pas le code de la route.
